instrument_date: n/a
competent_authority: none designated for a sandbox. The RTR KI-Servicestelle (AI Service Desk) exists but its statutory basis — § 20c KOG and § 194a TKG, inserted by BGBl. I Nr. 6/2024 — gives it an advisory/information-hub mandate only, not sandbox operation. Austria had also not designated its Art. 70 market surveillance or notifying authorities as of mid-2026.
sectors_in_scope: n/a — no instrument. A Wirtschaftskammer Österreich (WKO) white paper of 5 Feb 2026 proposes a sector-neutral sandbox naming health, industry, mobility, energy, education, public administration and critical infrastructure as relevant domains, with political responsibility at the Bundeskanzleramt and oversight by existing sectoral authorities. This is a business-chamber proposal, not government policy.
notes: No operational sandbox and no national instrument as of Sept 2026. The RTR AI Service Desk's own AI Act pages and FAQ describe the Art. 57 obligation generically and record the Omnibus postponement of the sandbox deadline, but say nothing about an Austrian sandbox, an authority, or a draft. The Digital Austria government AI Act page likewise covers only Art. 77 fundamental-rights authority designation. The WKO white paper (5 Feb 2026) and its companion article (5 May 2026) state explicitly that Austria has no dedicated legal framework, no designated authority and no government draft — that negative is the strongest evidence here, and it comes from an advocacy source rather than government, which is why confidence is medium not high. A May 2025 secondary source describes Austria as 'evaluating the concept through its AI Service Desk'; that is stale and unconfirmed by any RTR or federal source. Coded nothing_reported rather than announced because no government body has publicly committed to establishing one. Gap for the paper: no primary Austrian government statement of intent either way was found — worth a direct query to RTR/BKA before publication.

BIPT/IBPT (Belgian Institute for Postal Services and Telecommunications) is expected to become the principal market surveillance authority per the Federal Coalition Agreement 2025-2029, but this requires parliamentary approval that had not happened.
sectors_in_scope: n/a — no instrument
notes: No operational sandbox, no national instrument, and no designated authority as of late July 2026 (VRT NWS, 29 July 2026, quoting FPS Economy). A federal implementing bill was reported as in development but not yet before parliament; no text or title was traceable to a primary source, so it is not recorded as an instrument. Federal-structure caveat matters for the paper: Belgium's AI Act competence is split between the federal level and the communities/regions, which is the stated reason for the delay. Earlier signals are all pre-instrument and advisory: Senate written question 8-19 (18 Dec 2024) drew a ministerial answer that analysis was ongoing with a political decision expected 'at the earliest from February 2025' and made no mention of a sandbox; the FARI Institute / Kenniscentrum Data & Maatschappij event of 17 Dec 2024 presented academic 'recommendations for creating an AI regulatory sandbox in Belgium', i.e. a proposal, not a commitment. A Council of Ministers decision of 24 April 2026 does concern AI but is an unrelated bill on AI use by intelligence and security services — do not miscite it as AI Act implementation. Note the FPS Economy AI Act pages (economie.fgov.be/en|fr/themes/enterprises/ai-act) could not be retrieved (robots.txt), so their current content is unverified; a manual check is advisable before publication.

suff_funding_note: 2026 project proposal of EUR 213,520 for capacity and a regulatory laboratory, rated LOW PRIORITY by the Ministry of Finance and unfunded.
legal_instrument: none found. Two things are often miscited as instruments and are not: (1) the private member's bill 'Законопроект за използването и развитието на изкуствения интелект' (Bill on the Use and Development of Artificial Intelligence), tabled by MP Bozhidar Bozhanov (Da, Bulgaria) on 8 Oct 2025, which contained provisions for 'регулаторни лаборатории' (regulatory laboratories) but was REJECTED at first reading by the National Assembly's Committee on Electronic Governance and Information Technologies on 27 Nov 2025, the Ministry of Electronic Governance opposing it on 22 grounds; (2) a 2026 budget project proposal for 'administrative capacity and a regulatory laboratory for AI', budgeted at EUR 213,520, which the Ministry of Finance rated LOW PRIORITY.
instrument_date: n/a
competent_authority: none designated. The Ministry of Electronic Governance (Министерство на електронното управление, MEG) is the designated lead for AI Act implementation and coordinates an inter-ministerial working group tasked with producing the national framework (target March 2026). MEG had drafted a proposal to designate the Bulgarian Accreditation Service as the national notifying body, not approved by the Council of Ministers as of Jan 2026. No market surveillance authority designated; MEG stated Bulgaria 'still has no oversight of high-risk AI systems'.
sectors_in_scope: n/a — no instrument
notes: Coded 'announced' on the strength of a documented, government-side intention: MEG disclosed in an official FOI response (16-22 Dec 2025) and to the state news agency BTA (9 Jan 2026) a 2026 project proposal to build administrative capacity and a regulatory laboratory for AI. Read that coding with the caveat that the proposal was rated low priority by the Ministry of Finance and is unfunded — a reader applying a stricter definition of 'public commitment' could defensibly recode this to nothing_reported, and the paper should say which convention it uses. MEG identified insufficient expert capacity, missing technical infrastructure and institutional coordination as the obstacles. The rejected Bozhanov bill is the only Bulgarian text found containing sandbox provisions; its specific articles were not retrievable from a primary source, so no article numbers are asserted here. No post-January-2026 primary source on Bulgarian progress was found, so the March 2026 working-group target is unverified as met or missed — a marked gap.

legal_instrument: none found. A 'Zakon o provedbi uredbe (EU) 2024/1689 ... (Akt o umjetnoj inteligenciji)' appears on the government's e-Savjetovanja portal only as a legislative-activity consultation form (entityId 29348); the page could not be retrieved (404 on fetch), so neither its dates nor its content are verified, and no draft text, adoption or Narodne novine publication was found.
instrument_date: n/a
competent_authority: none designated for a sandbox, and no Art. 70 market surveillance or notifying authority designated as of July 2026. The Ministry of Justice, Administration and Digital Transformation (MPUDT) is preparing the national framework; the Central State Office for the Development of Digital Society represented Croatia at the AI Board. Separately, MPUDT published a list of Art. 77 fundamental-rights authorities on 5 Dec 2024 (Ombudswoman; Ombudswoman for Children; for Gender Equality; for Persons with Disabilities; AZOP/data protection agency; State Election Commission; Agency for Electronic Media) — this is Art. 77 designation only and must not be cited as sandbox or market-surveillance designation.
sectors_in_scope: n/a — no instrument
notes: Croatia is the least-documented of the four. As of 20 July 2026 there was no adopted implementing law, no designated regulator, and sandbox parameters were explicitly still open — CroAI's Stefan Martinic framed 'sto ce biti s regulatornim pjescanicima' (what will happen with the regulatory sandboxes) as a question for forthcoming legislation, and noted Croatia was roughly a year behind on the August 2025 authority-designation deadline. Industry commentary flags fragmentation risk across HAKOM, AZOP and HANFA. No Croatian government source found that mentions a sandbox at all. Two verification gaps worth closing before publication: the e-Savjetovanja consultation entry (esavjetovanja.gov.hr/ECon/MainScreen?entityId=29348) needs a manual look, and a Narodne novine search should be re-run close to submission in case an instrument lands. Croatia is not individually named in the EPRS April 2026 state-of-play note, which places it among the 16 member states that had not communicated sandbox plans.

legal_instrument: none found — no national AI Act implementing law has been enacted or even put to public consultation as of mid-2026; authority designation was made by Council of Ministers decision (reported as January 2025), not by statute
instrument_date: unknown (Council of Ministers governance decision reported as January 2025; no sandbox instrument)
competent_authority: Commissioner of Communications (Επίτροπος Επικοινωνιών / OCECPR) — designated Notifying Authority, Market Surveillance Authority and national Single Point of Contact per the European Commission's AI Act Service Desk national-resources listing. The Commissioner for Personal Data Protection has a parallel role for data-protection aspects. No authority has been designated to operate a sandbox.
sectors_in_scope: n/a — no sandbox established
notes: No Cypriot sandbox found in any source. Two independent Cypriot press reports (Ink/Offsite, 30 June 2026; Sigmalive, 12 August 2026) both report that Cyprus has no AI Act implementing bill: the Legal Service is quoted saying 'δεν υπάρχει αυτή τη στιγμή νομοσχέδιο' (no bill currently exists), and the Data Protection Commissioner is quoted saying the framework remains under formation because the techno-economic study commissioned by the Deputy Ministry of Research, Innovation and Digital Policy is unfinished and the bill has not gone to public consultation. Neither article mentions a sandbox. The official ai.cy portal (run by the Commissioner of Communications) states only the obligation itself — that member states must have at least one sandbox operational by 02/08/2027, which independently confirms Cyprus is working to the post-Omnibus deadline. CAVEAT for the paper: the two Cypriot press reports differ on the division of roles — the June 2026 report describes the Communications Commissioner as coordination point and the DPA as market surveillance authority, while the August 2026 report and the Commission's own Service Desk listing give the Communications Commissioner the notifying, market-surveillance and SPOC roles. I have followed the Commission Service Desk as the authoritative source. Cite Cyprus as a confirmed gap, not as an unresearched one.

legal_instrument: No adopted AI-specific national instrument. (a) Sandbox operatorship was assigned administratively by the government-approved 'Plán implementace AI Actu v ČR' (government approval 28 May 2025). (b) A draft adaptation law (návrh zákona o umělé inteligenci, prepared by the Ministry of Industry and Trade / MPO, draft published 12 January 2026) contains the sandbox provisions but had not been adopted as of the latest sourcing. (c) Act No. 328/2025 Coll. on research, development, innovation and knowledge transfer provides a general, non-AI-specific statutory regulatory-sandbox framework.
instrument_date: Government implementation plan approved 28 May 2025; MPO draft AI law published 12 January 2026 (not adopted); Act 328/2025 Coll. enacted 2025
competent_authority: Czech Agency for Standardization (Česká agentura pro standardizaci, ČAS) operates the sandbox; the Office for Technical Standardization, Metrology and State Testing (ÚNMZ) is its founder and the notifying authority. Separately, the Czech Telecommunication Office (ČTÚ) is the general market surveillance authority and SPOC, with the Czech National Bank (financial sector) and the Office for Personal Data Protection (ÚOOÚ, biometrics/law-enforcement high-risk) as co-supervisors.
sectors_in_scope: Cross-sectoral in design. Reporting emphasises automotive/autonomous systems and advanced analytics; the government implementation-plan coverage also names biometric identification, visa processing and medical robotics among high-risk applications generally. SME-oriented.
notes: Do NOT code Czechia as operational. Lupa.cz (12 May 2026) reported the sandbox was scheduled to launch 'during this August' (2026) under ČAS with MPO funding making it free for startups, and that entry is not automatic — a selection process applies. I could find no source confirming the launch actually happened, no ČAS application call, and no ČAS sandbox page (a site search of agenturacas.gov.cz returned nothing on AI sandboxes). Treat 'implementing' as the defensible coding: the operator is designated and a draft instrument exists, but neither operation nor the instrument is confirmed. On entry criteria: the draft law reportedly delegates the criteria to ČAS, which is to publish them on its website, and entry requires a signed agreement with no right to admission — so criteria are provided for but not (yet) published. Legislative status is a live risk: the draft was in inter-ministerial review in Feb 2026 and expected to go to government before 2 August 2026; a Czech government change followed the October 2025 election, and I found no confirmation of adoption. TRAP FLAGGED: Act No. 328/2025 Coll. is titled 'o výzkumu, vývoji, inovacích a transferu znalostí' (research, development, innovation and knowledge transfer) — it is a general innovation/sandbox framework, NOT the AI Act sandbox instrument. A consultancy tracker (regulatornisandboxy.cz, AQE advisors) presents it alongside the AI Act and still states the sandbox deadline as August 2026, i.e. it is pre-Omnibus and stale; I could not read the statute text directly (zakonyprolidi.cz and e-sbirka.gov.cz both blocked machine fetch), so do not cite 328/2025 as the AI sandbox basis without reading the text.

verification_note: Refuted. Operational GDPR/data-protection sandbox (est. March 2024), not constituted under Art. 57. No Danish instrument creates an Art. 57 sandbox.
derogation_power_note: Administrative GDPR-sandbox programme; guidance only, no derogation power.
suff_graduation_note: Final reports are required and published as a programme rule, not as a statutory Art. 57(7) obligation.
suff_recognition_note: Not constituted under Art. 57, so Art. 58(2) does not attach.
legal_instrument: None found for the sandbox itself. The Danish AI Act implementing statute is Lov nr. 467 af 14. maj 2025 om supplerende bestemmelser til forordningen om kunstig intelligens (in force 2 August 2025), which designates authorities and sanctions but contains no sandbox provisions. The sandbox is established administratively by Datatilsynet and Digitaliseringsstyrelsen as part of the government's digitalisation strategy.
instrument_date: Lov nr. 467 of 14 May 2025 (in force 2 August 2025) — authority designation only, no sandbox provision. Sandbox itself has no dated legal instrument; first round announced 8 July 2024.
competent_authority: Jointly operated by Datatilsynet (Danish Data Protection Authority) and Digitaliseringsstyrelsen (Danish Agency for Digital Government). Under Lov nr. 467/2025, Digitaliseringsstyrelsen is the central contact point, notifying authority and coordinating market surveillance authority; Datatilsynet is market surveillance authority for Art. 5(1)(d) and (g); Domstolsstyrelsen for court use of AI.
sectors_in_scope: Cross-sectoral. Any actual or potential AI-system provider — companies, public authorities and other organisations — may apply; the programme explicitly contemplates drawing in sectoral regulators where health law (sundhedsloven), social legislation or employment law intersects with data protection and the AI Act.
participants: 7 projects across three rounds: round 1 (announced 8 July 2024) — 2 projects from 23 applications (Tryg Forsikring; Systematic with Copenhagen, Aarhus and Aalborg municipalities, the 'Talt' health/elderly-care documentation project); round 2 (announced 18 June 2025) — 2 projects from 18 applications (Børns Vilkår; BrainCapture ApS); round 3 (announced 9 July 2026) — 3 projects (Lex – Danmarks Nationalleksikon; Kintella ApS with Region Hovedstaden; Fenja ApS).
adversarial_verification: REFUTED -> Operational-but-not-Article-57. A Danish AI regulatory sandbox is genuinely admitting and hosting participants (three rounds to date), but it is an administratively established GDPR/data-protection sandbox created in March 2024 under the government's digitalisation strategy — not a sandbox constituted under EU AI Act Article 57. For Article 57 purposes Denmark's status is "not established": no Danish legal instrument creates an Art. 57 sandbox, neither Lov nr. 467 af 14. maj 2025 nor the amending AI-loven (L 111, 2025/26, in force 2 August 2026) contains any sandbox provision, and there is no Art. 57(7) exit-report or Art. 57(9) legal-certainty mechanism.
notes: Denmark is the strongest case in this set and the most useful for a healthcare-AI paper — health/medical AI is not merely eligible but repeatedly admitted: round 1 included Systematic's 'Talt' voice-to-text documentation project for health and elderly care with three municipalities; round 2 included BrainCapture ApS, a MedTech startup using AI to interpret EEG for diagnosing epilepsy and other neurological conditions; round 3 (announced 9 July 2026) included Kintella ApS with Region Hovedstaden, covering AI translation between health personnel and citizens plus decision support for early detection of patient deterioration. IMPORTANT NUANCE for the paper — do not conflate the operational sandbox with an Article 57 legal designation. The Danish sandbox predates the AI Act sandbox obligation (first round July 2024) and is an administrative programme run out of the government's digitalisation strategy; Digitaliseringsstyrelsen now hosts it under its AI Act supervision pages (digst.dk/tilsyn/ai-forordningen/), but neither authority's page cites Article 57 by number, and I found no national instrument designating it as the Art. 57 sandbox. Exit reports: final reports (slutrapporter) ARE required and published as a condition of the programme — reports from round 1 were published in October 2025 — but this is a programme rule, not a statutory Art. 57(7) obligation, which is why I code exit_report_required as 'no' at the instrument level. Legislative gap to flag: bill L 111 (2025-26), 'Forslag til lov om supplerende bestemmelser til forordningen om kunstig intelligens (AI-loven)', presented 18 February 2026 and given its first reading 17 March 2026, is recorded by Folketingstidende as 'Bortfaldet' (lapsed) — consistent with a 2026 Danish general election (a new Folketing membership list for 2026– exists). That bill also appeared to contain no sandbox provisions. So as of September 2026 Denmark has an operational sandbox with no bespoke statutory basis. Entry criteria are published on both authorities' sites: Danish-society relevance, a genuine AI system as defined in the AI Act, coverage by the AI Act and/or GDPR, applicant is a provider or potential provider, and maturity beyond concept stage; selection then weighs societal significance, innovation potential, benefit from participation, economic feasibility and learning value for others. Round-3 timing: applications closed 1 May 2026, intro meetings June 2026, sandbox activity September–December 2026.

legal_instrument: none found — no AI-specific national instrument. The nearest vehicle is a draft amendment to the General Part of the Economic Activities Code Act and the State Fees Act (Majandustegevuse seadustiku üldosa seaduse ja riigilõivuseaduse muutmise seadus), explanatory memorandum dated 10 November 2025, which would create a general cross-sectoral regulatory sandbox framework — not an AI Act Article 57 sandbox. I found no confirmation it has been adopted.
instrument_date: Draft explanatory memorandum 10 November 2025; adoption not confirmed
competent_authority: Not designated for a sandbox. Under the draft general sandbox framework, the Ministry of Economic Affairs and Communications (MKM) would do initial screening and the competent sectoral regulator (pädev majandushaldusasutus) would decide admission. For the AI Act more broadly, Estonia's official Kratid portal records three bodies designated under Article 77: the Data Protection Inspectorate (Andmekaitse Inspektsioon), the Gender Equality and Equal Treatment Commissioner, and the Consumer Protection and Technical Regulatory Authority (TTJA). TTJA is the de facto market-surveillance body.
sectors_in_scope: n/a for an AI sandbox. The draft general framework is cross-sectoral, applying only where a sectoral law expressly refers to it.
notes: Estonia is the weakest evidence base of the four — code it low confidence and consider marking it a gap rather than a data point. What supports 'announced' rather than 'nothing_reported': a joint Finland–Estonia announcement (reported 20 May 2026) that the two governments agreed to jointly develop regulatory sandboxes, with both expected to report AI Act sandbox implementation progress by end-2026 — but the joint press release named no AI systems, policy areas, timelines or funding. What is absent: no AI-specific law, no designated sandbox operator, no application process, no participants. Estonia's official AI portal (kratid.ee) discusses the AI Regulation and Article 77 authority designations but says nothing about a sandbox. The draft MSÜS/State Fees amendment is a genuinely useful comparator for the paper but must not be mislabelled: its own explanatory memorandum acknowledges the Article 57 obligation and notes MKM as contact point, yet the bill builds a general innovation sandbox (criteria: innovative product/service with economic or social benefit, a demonstrated regulatory barrier, a risk-mitigation plan, alternative compliance routes, and a public-interest assessment) with a post-project reporting duty — participants file with MKM within 30 days of closure and MKM publishes a summary assessing whether regulatory change is needed. That reporting duty resembles but is not the Art. 57(7) exit report, and healthcare/medical AI is mentioned only in passing via Accelerate Estonia projects. Two further cautions: (1) I could not load TTJA's own AI-systems page (repeated 503/permission failures) — a follow-up check there is the single highest-value verification step for Estonia; (2) the trackers disagree — artificialintelligenceact.eu (last updated 17 June 2026) records Estonia as having no implementation law and authorities 'not yet appointed', which conflicts with kratid.ee's Article 77 designations, and regulatoryai.eu (reviewed 14 June 2026) says Estonia plans sandbox facilities through an 'AI competence centre' that 'does not yet operate' — but that page still prints the pre-Omnibus 2 August 2026 sandbox deadline and is therefore stale and unusable as a source of record.

legal_instrument: No enacted national instrument establishing the sandbox as of 8 Sept 2026. The in-force base act is Laki eräiden tekoälyjärjestelmien valvonnasta (Act on the Supervision of Certain AI Systems) 1377/2025, enacted from HE 46/2025 vp (submitted 8 May 2025), supervisory powers in force 1 Jan 2026 — but it designates authorities and sanctions only and contains NO sandbox provisions. The sandbox provisions sit in a pending phase-II amendment bill, project TEM091:00/2024 ("tekoälyasetuksen II vaiheen täytäntöönpano"), consultation 25 Apr – 2 Jun 2025, government proposal to Parliament 29 Jan 2026, planned entry into force 1 March 2027. No corresponding 2026 amendment act was found in Finlex, so it appears still before the Eduskunta.
instrument_date: Act 1377/2025 (base act, supervisory powers in force 1 Jan 2026); phase-II sandbox bill to Parliament 29 Jan 2026, planned in force 1 March 2027 — not yet enacted
competent_authority: Liikenne- ja viestintävirasto (Traficom), the Finnish Transport and Communications Agency. Traficom is already the central market-surveillance contact point under 1377/2025 and is the body proposed to run the testiympäristö in the phase-II draft; it maintains a public page titled "Tekoälyn sääntelyn testiympäristöt".
sectors_in_scope: Not specified. Neither the draft nor Traficom's page enumerates sectors. The Finnish Competition and Consumer Authority (KKV), in its 28 May 2025 consultation opinion, expressly flagged that it was unclear whether the sandbox would cover only Annex III high-risk systems or a broader set, and pressed for consumer-facing and generative AI to be included.
notes: Classified 'implementing' because an authority (Traficom) is designated and publicly holds the brief, and a government proposal is before Parliament — but be precise in the paper: Finland has NO enacted sandbox instrument. Planned entry into force is 1 March 2027, i.e. Finland is deliberately tracking the post-Omnibus 2 Aug 2027 deadline rather than the old 2026 one. I could not retrieve the phase-II HE number or confirm its parliamentary stage as of Sept 2026 — Finlex and Eduskunta document pages returned only navigation shells. Also note Fimea (medicines agency) is among the ~18 sectoral authorities designated under the phase-I act, but that is market surveillance, not sandbox operation. Gaps to close before citing: (1) the phase-II HE number and current committee stage; (2) whether the draft's sandbox section names sectors or an exit report.

legal_instrument: none found
instrument_date: n/a
competent_authority: None designated for a sandbox. For AI Act market surveillance generally, France has announced a distributed, sectoral architecture (~15 bodies) with DGCCRF as coordinator and CNIL in a central role, alongside Arcom, ACPR, ANSSI and sector regulators — but this architecture is set out in a bill that is not yet law, and no body has been designated to operate an Article 57 sandbox.
sectors_in_scope: n/a — no sandbox established
notes: France is the clear laggard of the four and is a useful negative case for the paper. The vehicle is the projet de loi DDADUE, texte n° 118 (2025-2026), deposited in the Sénat 10 Nov 2025 under accelerated procedure; Article 24 concerns Regulation (EU) 2024/1689. The Sénat adopted it 18 Feb 2026 (texte n° 63), transmitted to the Assemblée nationale 20 Feb 2026 (texte n° 2518); as of the dossier's 4 Sept 2026 update it remains in first reading at the Assemblée and is NOT promulgated. Critically, the bill's étude d'impact contains no mention of a bac à sable réglementaire or Articles 57-63 at all — the French instrument, as drafted, addresses authority designation only, not the sandbox mandate. CAUTION for citation: CNIL runs several things it calls a « bac à sable » (AI in public services, digital health, edtech) — these are GDPR/personal-data sandboxes predating and legally distinct from the AI Act Article 57 sandbox, and conflating them would be a factual error. Arcep separately runs a telecoms 'bac à sable réglementaire' that is also unrelated. Also flag that the DGE's own explainer page (last updated 28 July 2025) still states sandboxes must be in place by 2 August 2026 — stale, pre-Omnibus, do not cite for the deadline.

derogation_power_note: Sec. 13 KI-MIG requires BNetzA to establish a sandbox under Arts. 57-58; no derogation power identified in the provision as read from the Regierungsentwurf.
suff_graduation_note: Sec. 13 KI-MIG contains no Art. 57(7) provision; left to the directly applicable Regulation and a forthcoming BMDS Rechtsverordnung.
suff_recognition_note: Sec. 13(1) KI-MIG requires a sandbox 'nach den Artikeln 57 und 58' - Art. 58 reached by cross-reference, not restated.
legal_instrument: Gesetz zur Marktüberwachung und Innovationsförderung von künstlicher Intelligenz (KI-Marktüberwachungs- und Innovationsförderungsgesetz, KI-MIG), enacted as Article 1 of the Gesetz zur Durchführung der Verordnung (EU) 2024/1689. § 13 KI-MIG ("KI-Reallabore; Verordnungsermächtigung") is the operative sandbox provision: § 13(1) — "Die Bundesnetzagentur errichtet und betreibt mindestens ein KI-Reallabor nach den Artikeln 57 und 58 der Verordnung (EU) 2024/1689."
instrument_date: Cabinet (Regierungsentwurf) 10/11 Feb 2026; Bundestag adoption 11 June 2026; published Bundesgesetzblatt 2026 I Nr. 233 on 28 July 2026; in force 29 July 2026
competent_authority: Bundesnetzagentur (BNetzA). § 13(2) requires BNetzA to cooperate with other authorities where the establishment or operation of the Reallabor touches their competence, so sector-specific regulators participate rather than run parallel statutory sandboxes.
sectors_in_scope: No sectoral enumeration in § 13 — it applies generally to AI systems within the scope of Reg. (EU) 2024/1689. § 13(3) grants priority access ("vorrangigen Zugang") to research institutions and startups meeting specified criteria; § 13(4) empowers the BMDS to set the detailed rules on establishment and operation by Rechtsverordnung (no Bundesrat consent required).
participants: 0 in the statutory sandbox — it is not yet operational. Separately, BNetzA ran a trilateral simulation 'Pilotprojekt KI-Reallabor' (May 2025 – March 2026) with the Hessian Ministry for Digitalisation and the BfDI; that was an exploratory simulation, not admission of real participants.
notes: Germany is the strongest 'law passed, sandbox not yet running' case of the four. BNetzA's own KI-Reallabore page states the obligation is to have at least one sandbox operational by 2 August 2027 — i.e. BNetzA has already publicly adopted the post-Omnibus deadline, which is a citable data point that German authorities are treating Reg. (EU) 2026/1744 as operative. Health-AI relevance for your paper, but state it carefully: § 13 does NOT name medical or health AI. What IS documented is that the completed pilot project produced a roadmap setting out high-risk AI Act requirements specifically for AI-based medical devices — so healthcare was the pilot's worked example without being a statutory scope category. On the exit report: § 13 contains no Art. 57(7) exit-report provision; the KI-MIG leaves it to the directly applicable EU regulation and to the forthcoming BMDS Rechtsverordnung. Entry criteria are not published because they are delegated to that Rechtsverordnung, which had not been issued as of the sources consulted. VERIFICATION CAVEAT: § 13's text was read from the Regierungsentwurf PDF (BMDS, 9/10 Feb 2026); gesetze-im-internet.de blocked automated retrieval, so I could not confirm that the section number and wording survived unchanged into the promulgated text. Verify § 13 against gesetze-im-internet.de/ki-mig or the BGBl before citing the section number. Also note a separate EU-funded pilot, EUSAiR, accepting up to 90 use cases Oct 2025 – June 2026 open to all sectors and sizes — that is an EU programme, not a German national Art. 57 sandbox, and should not be counted as one.

legal_instrument: Νόμος 5321/2026, «Μέτρα εφαρμογής του Κανονισμού (ΕΕ) 2024/1689 του Ευρωπαϊκού Κοινοβουλίου και του Συμβουλίου της 13ης Ιουνίου 2024 (Κανονισμός για την τεχνητή νοημοσύνη) — Τροποποίηση του ν. 4961/2022». Article 12 («Ρυθμιστικό δοκιμαστήριο τεχνητής νοημοσύνης») establishes the sandbox.
instrument_date: ΦΕΚ Α΄ 114/20.07.2026 — published and in force 20 July 2026. Public consultation on the draft ran 21 June – 6 July 2026 (Ministry of Digital Governance, opengov.gr).
competent_authority: EETT (Εθνική Επιτροπή Τηλεπικοινωνιών και Ταχυδρομείων / Hellenic Telecommunications and Post Commission) establishes and operates the sandbox, jointly designated with the APDPX (Αρχή Προστασίας Δεδομένων Προσωπικού Χαρακτήρα / Hellenic Data Protection Authority), with relevant sectoral authorities participating. Separately, the APDPX is designated as central market surveillance authority and national single point of contact under the same law.
sectors_in_scope: Not enumerated. Article 12 refers generically to Articles 57-59 of Reg. (EU) 2024/1689 without sectoral limitation. Article 12(3) requires EETT to issue a call (πρόσκληση) fixing application deadlines, content and format of applications, scoring criteria, a cap on participants, fees, and any other matter needed to implement Arts. 57-59 that is not covered by EU delegated acts. The law also states that sandbox participation is not a general exemption from the AI Act, the GDPR or other applicable law.
participants: unknown — none published; no EETT call located
notes: Greece has the sandbox in enacted primary law, which is a stronger position than Finland or France, but it is not operational: the criteria and the admission mechanism are entirely delegated to an EETT πρόσκληση, and no such call was found on EETT's site or in any official announcement as of 8 Sept 2026. Article 12 sets no deadline for the sandbox to be running. WARNING on secondary sources: a 5 Sept 2026 Greek news piece (anagnostis.org) headlined that the sandbox 'arrives in Greece' — it misstates the law number as 5317/2026, gives the passage date as 16 July 2026, treats the superseded 2 August 2026 deadline as live, and describes EETT as merely the 'notifying authority'. Do not cite it; its claims conflict with the FEK-published text. The reliable pairing is the enacted-law text (ΦΕΚ Α΄ 114/20.07.2026) plus the Ministry of Digital Governance announcement. Gaps to close: (1) whether Art. 12 or a later provision of L. 5321/2026 restates the Art. 57(7) exit report — two independent reads of Art. 12 found no reference, but I only read Art. 12, not the full law; (2) whether an EETT call has since issued. I read Art. 12 in the consultation draft PDF and cross-checked against a legal commentary on the enacted law; the two agree on authority, delegation structure and absence of sectoral scope, so those three points are solid.

suff_graduation_note: Sec. 10 delegates operative rules to a ministerial decree that could not be found as adopted; no Art. 57(7) provision in the Act.
legal_instrument: 2025. évi LXXV. törvény az Európai Unió mesterséges intelligenciáról szóló rendeletének magyarországi végrehajtásáról (Act LXXV of 2025 on the domestic implementation of the EU AI Regulation), promulgated 31 October 2025 — §10 is the sandbox provision. Accompanied by 344/2025. (X. 31.) Korm. rendelet (Government Decree 344/2025 of 31 October 2025), which designates the authorities. The ministerial decree containing the detailed sandbox rules, mandated by §10(2) and §11(3), could not be found as adopted.
instrument_date: Act LXXV of 2025 promulgated 31 October 2025; general entry into force 1 December 2025 (31st day after promulgation, §12(1)); §10 (sandbox) entered into force 2 August 2026 (§12(2)). Government Decree 344/2025 dated 31 October 2025.
competent_authority: MI piacfelügyeleti hatóság (AI market surveillance authority) = a vállalkozásfejlesztésért felelős miniszter — the Minister responsible for business development, designated by §1(1) of Government Decree 344/2025. (The MI bejelentő hatóság / notifying authority is the Nemzeti Akkreditáló Hatóság, National Accreditation Authority, but it is the market surveillance authority that §10(1) charges with establishing and operating the sandbox.)
sectors_in_scope: Not specified. §10 of Act LXXV/2025 contains no sectoral scoping; §10(2) defers all detail — including the participation of other authorities — to a ministerial decree not yet located as adopted. §10(3) provides only that state-held high-performance computing capacity may be ring-fenced for the minister to run the sandbox.
notes: CAUTION ON THE STATUS CALL. The legal framework is confirmed from the Hungarian national law gazette (Nemzeti Jogszabálytár), which is primary. §10(1) reads verbatim: 'Az MI piacfelügyeleti hatóság az (EU) 2024/1689 európai parlamenti és tanácsi rendelet 3. cikk 55. pontjában meghatározott, az 57. cikk szerinti MI szabályozói tesztkörnyezetet alakít ki és működtet.' §10(2): 'Az MI szabályozói tesztkörnyezet működésének részletes szabályait ... a miniszter rendeletben állapítja meg.' So the duty to build and run a sandbox is in force (since 2 August 2026), but the operative rules are delegated to a ministerial decree I could NOT find evidence of. The 'implementing, not operational' classification therefore rests partly on absence of evidence — I found no call for applications, no published criteria, no admitted participants, and no launch announcement. For a FaccT submission I would either mark this as a verified gap or have a Hungarian-reading colleague check Magyar Közlöny 2026 issues directly for a 'miniszteri rendelet' on the MI szabályozói tesztkörnyezet; my searches of Magyar Közlöny returned nothing. Two secondary trackers I checked are badly stale (Bird & Bird's Hungary tracker last updated 30 June 2025) and should not be cited. Separately: net.jogtar.hu and njt.hu were blocked by the egress proxy, so I relied on njt.jog.gov.hu, which is the same official Nemzeti Jogszabálytár service. On the Omnibus: kormany.hu confirmed on 29 July 2026 that member states now have until August 2027 for sandboxes ('a tagállamoknak a szabályozói tesztkörnyezetek (AI sandboxok) kialakítására is több idő jut, egészen 2027 augusztusáig'), but Hungary has NOT correspondingly amended §12(2) of its own Act — the national §10 commencement date of 2 August 2026 still stands, which is a genuinely interesting divergence for the paper: Hungary is late against its own national deadline, not merely against the (now-extended) EU one.

legal_instrument: Regulation of Artificial Intelligence Act 2026 (No. 31 of 2026). Sandbox provisions are in Part 3, Chapter 3, sections 46–47. Section 46 provides that 'The Office shall establish one or more AI regulatory sandboxes', with detailed rules to be set by Ministerial regulations. Predecessor instrument: General Scheme of the Regulation of Artificial Intelligence Bill 2026, published 4 February 2026 (sandbox at Head 35).
instrument_date: General Scheme published 4 February 2026; Bill published 17 June 2026; passed all stages in Dáil Éireann 30 June 2026 and Seanad Éireann thereafter; signed into law by President Connolly on 21 July 2026.
competent_authority: Oifig IS na hÉireann / the AI Office of Ireland, established under the Act. Paul Byrne appointed as first CEO (announced 30 July 2026); board members approved 5 August 2026. Note the AI Office is the single point of contact and central coordinating authority — the market surveillance function was deliberately removed from it between the General Scheme and the published Bill, but responsibility for establishing and operating the sandbox remained with the Office.
sectors_in_scope: Not specified in the Act. Sections 46–47 impose no sectoral limits; the Act provides for priority access for SMEs and start-ups with a registered office or branch in the EU, and defers 'conditions and criteria for the assessment and selection of applicants' to Ministerial regulations that have not yet been made.
notes: Status is well established and the 'not operational' finding is positively confirmed rather than inferred: the AI Office of Ireland's own sandbox page states 'Details on eligibility and the application process will be made available when the Sandbox has been developed.' That is a first-party statement from the designated authority that the sandbox does not yet exist, which is the strongest possible evidence for a nothing-yet finding — cite that page. TWO CAVEATS. (1) I could not read the enacted text of Act No. 31 of 2026 directly: irishstatutebook.ie returned 403 through the agent proxy on both curl and WebFetch, and oireachtas.ie likewise. My account of sections 46–47 therefore comes from the Oireachtas Library & Research Service Bill Digest (8 July 2026), which is an official parliamentary publication but describes the Bill as published on 17 June 2026, NOT the Act as enacted on 21 July 2026 — amendments at Seanad committee stage could have changed the section numbering or content. Before citing section numbers in the paper, verify against irishstatutebook.ie/eli/2026/act/31/enacted/en/html from an unblocked connection. (2) Exit report is marked 'unknown' rather than 'no' for the same reason: the Bill Digest records no Article 57(7) exit-report provision in sections 46–47, but the Act delegates sandbox detail to Ministerial regulations, so the obligation may be intended to sit there. Also note the Bill Digest itself states the establishment deadline as 2 August 2026 per Article 57 — it is dated 8 July 2026, the same day the Digital Omnibus was adopted, so it is stale on that point and should not be cited for the deadline.

suff_graduation_note: Art. 31 of the draft decree requires annual reports and a final report from national authorities to the AI Office - that maps to Art. 57(6), not Art. 57(7).
legal_instrument: Two-layer. Framework/enabling law: Legge 23 settembre 2025, n. 132 (published Gazzetta Ufficiale Serie Generale n. 223, in force 10 October 2025), which delegates implementation to legislative decrees. The sandbox itself is created by a schema di decreto legislativo on the powers of national authorities, market surveillance, sanctions, experimentation spaces, training and labour — transmitted to Parliament as Atto del Governo n. 421 (a companion decree on policing and liability is AG n. 418). Sandbox provisions are at Articles 26–31 of that schema; Article 26 establishes the 'spazio di sperimentazione normativa per l'IA'.
instrument_date: Law 132/2025 dated 23 September 2025, in force 10 October 2025. The implementing legislative decree: preliminary Council of Ministers approval 10 June 2026; parliamentary committee opinions July 2026 (Garante privacy opinion 14 July 2026; Senate 4th Committee 29 July 2026); definitive Council of Ministers approval 4–5 August 2026. Publication in the Gazzetta Ufficiale — and therefore the decree's number and entry into force — NOT confirmed as of 8 September 2026.
competent_authority: AgID (Agenzia per l'Italia Digitale) and ACN (Agenzia per la Cybersicurezza Nazionale) jointly, each within its own competence — AgID as notifying authority, ACN as market surveillance authority. Under Law 132/2025 these two are the national AI authorities.
sectors_in_scope: The schema provides for a general AI sandbox (Art. 26) plus dedicated tracks: dual-use/defence AI and AI in the justice sector, a regional/local strand, and coordination with the existing FinTech sandbox. SMEs and start-ups receive priority access (Art. 26(1)). Eligibility criteria are to be identified and assessed under Art. 26(3) but are not themselves published.
notes: THE WEAKEST RECORD OF THE FOUR — do not treat the article numbers as citable without one more check. Key gap: I could not confirm that the legislative decree has been published in the Gazzetta Ufficiale. The most recent source addressing this (Federprivacy, post-4 August 2026) states explicitly 'Alla data di redazione non risulta ancora avvenuta la pubblicazione dei decreti nella Gazzetta Ufficiale.' So as of my research the sandbox's legal instrument has been definitively approved by the Council of Ministers but may not yet be law. Before the paper cites it, look up the decree number and GU issue on normattiva.it or gazzettaufficiale.it — I could not reach either through the proxy. Until then the instrument should be cited as 'schema di decreto legislativo, AG 421' and not as a numbered d.lgs. Second caution: my reading of Articles 26–31 came from a draft PDF hosted on a third-party CMS (storagehub.homnya.net), which is a reproduced draft, NOT a primary source — the article numbers and the Art. 31 reporting text must be re-verified against the official AG 421 text on the Camera/Senato atti del governo portal, and could have shifted between the June draft and the August final version. Third: the health question is genuinely contested in my sources. The draft text I read does not name sanità in the sandbox articles, while Agenda Digitale's 27 July 2026 analysis of AG 421 lists healthcare among the sectors the sandbox touches. I have coded 'not specified' because the conservative reading of the instrument text supports it, but flag this as unresolved. Fourth: on the exit report, Art. 31 of the draft requires annual reports and a 'relazione definitiva' from the national competent authorities to the AI Office — that maps onto AI Act Art. 57(6) (reporting to the AI Office and Commission), NOT Art. 57(7) (the exit report given to the participant on request). I found no Art. 57(7) transposition, but given the draft-text problem I have coded this 'unknown' rather than 'no'. Note also the Garante privacy's 14 July 2026 opinion made DPA involvement in sandbox projects processing personal data a condition of its approval — a useful data point for a healthcare-AI governance paper, since health sandbox projects would necessarily trigger it.

verification_note: Holds. Genuine Art. 57-era statutory sandbox; AI Centre issues administrative acts permitting derogation from national rules.
derogation_power_note: Art. 8 AI Centre Law: the Centre issues administrative acts permitting derogation from otherwise applicable national rules. Verified against likumi.lv.
suff_graduation_note: Point 27 of Cabinet Reg. No. 12 requires the sectorally competent authority, on the implementer's request, to issue an opinion on development and testing results - tracks Art. 57(7) including the on-request structure. Point 28 additionally requires the Centre to publish conclusions and recommendations, which Art. 57(7) does not.
legal_instrument: Two instruments. Primary: Mākslīgā intelekta centra likums (Law on the Artificial Intelligence Centre) — Articles 8 and 9 create the 'speciālā regulatīvā vide' (special regulatory environment) and the associated data-processing regime. Implementing: Ministru kabineta 2026. gada 13. janvāra noteikumi Nr. 12 'Kārtība, kādā Mākslīgā intelekta centrs organizē speciālo regulatīvo vidi un datu apstrādi' (Cabinet of Ministers Regulation No. 12 of 13 January 2026 on the procedure by which the AI Centre organises the special regulatory environment and data processing), issued under Articles 8(5) and 9(8) of that Law.
instrument_date: Mākslīgā intelekta centra likums adopted by the Saeima 6 March 2025; published Latvijas Vēstnesis No. 55, 19 March 2025; in force 20 March 2025. Cabinet Regulation No. 12 adopted 13 January 2026, in force 16 January 2026.
competent_authority: Nodibinājums 'Mākslīgā intelekta centrs' (the Artificial Intelligence Centre, MIC), operating under the Ministry of Smart Administration and Regional Development (VARAM), in cooperation with the sectorally competent supervisory authorities, which issue the assessments. Director: Guna Puce. Under Article 8 the Centre issues administrative acts permitting derogation from otherwise applicable national rules.
sectors_in_scope: Broad and cross-sectoral. Article 4 of the AI Centre Law lists application areas as 'valsts pārvaldē, tautsaimniecībā, iekšējās drošības, aizsardzības, izglītības, kultūras, labklājības, sporta, veselības un citās jomās' — public administration, the economy, internal security, defence, education, culture, welfare, sport, HEALTH and other fields. The first call flagged health, education and security as expected areas.
participants: 3 selected in the first call (out of 10 applications), announced May 2026: MyWisy (adaptive learning platform for pre-schoolers), ANIMAS-DA / 'Diabetes Assistant' (paediatric type 1 diabetes insulin-dosing decision support), and the Process-as-Code platform (public-administration decision automation). Of these, the AI Centre adopted its first administrative acts on 17 August 2026 for TWO high-risk systems — MyWisy and ANIMAS-DA — which are the two now formally operating inside the sandbox.
adversarial_verification:
HOLDS — WHAT I COULD VERIFY

1) The primary instrument exists. "Mākslīgā intelekta centra likums" is published on the official consolidated-law portal (https://likumi.lv/ta/id/359339-maksliga-intelekta-centra-likums) and in the official gazette Latvijas Vēstnesis 2025 No. 55 (https://www.vestnesis.lv/op/2025/55.1), matching the claimed 19 March 2025 publication. LV portāls (state-run legal information por
notes: STRONGEST RECORD OF THE FOUR, and by far the most useful for a healthcare-AI governance paper — Latvia is not merely operational but has a high-risk PAEDIATRIC MEDICAL AI system (ANIMAS-DA: continuous glucose monitoring data, insulin dosing recommendations for children with type 1 diabetes) formally admitted by administrative act. Both instruments verified against primary sources (vestnesis.lv for the Law, likumi.lv for Cabinet Regulation No. 12). One number to state carefully: 3 vs 2. LV portāls (12 May 2026) reports three projects selected from ten applications at the close of the first call; LSM English (6 Aug 2026) and Kursors (17 Aug 2026) report two systems actually launched/admitted by administrative act, both high-risk. The cleanest formulation for the paper is 'three projects selected in the first call, of which two — both high-risk — were formally admitted by administrative act as of 17 August 2026.' I could not determine what happened to Process-as-Code; most likely it is not high-risk and so needed no Article 8 administrative act, but I did not confirm that, so do not assert it. Entry criteria: published in point 9 of Cabinet Regulation No. 12 — newly created or substantially modified system, innovativeness, establishment in Latvia/EU/EEA/Switzerland, contribution to stated policy goals or correction of a market failure, system maturity, and risk level (high-risk systems prioritised). Exit report: point 27 of Reg. No. 12 requires the sectorally competent authority, ON THE PROJECT IMPLEMENTER'S REQUEST, to prepare an 'atzinums par mākslīgā intelekta sistēmas izstrādes, pārbaudes un attīstības rezultātiem' — an opinion on the development, testing and development results. That tracks AI Act Art. 57(7) closely, including the on-request structure. Point 28 goes further than Art. 57(7) requires: after activity in the sandbox concludes the Centre must prepare and PUBLISH on its website conclusions on the system's development and testing plus recommendations — a transparency obligation with no direct AI Act analogue, which is a genuinely publishable finding. Quote both points verbatim from likumi.lv rather than relying on my paraphrase.

suff_funding_note: EUR 3m from the ERDF, project period 30 Oct 2025 - 2 Nov 2028 (RRT).
suff_graduation_note: Ministry page describes written evidence of activities and a completion report usable in conformity assessment, but this is a programme description and was not shown to be a requirement of the national instrument.
legal_instrument: Law amending Articles 1, 2, 11, 13, 14, 17, 21 of the Law on Technology and Innovation No. XIII-1414 and supplementing the Law with an Annex (Lietuvos Respublikos technologijų ir inovacijų įstatymo Nr. XIII-1414 1, 2, 11, 13, 14, 17, 21 straipsnių pakeitimo ir Įstatymo papildymo priedu įstatymas), No. XV-105, adopted by the Seimas 14 January 2025, published TAR 22 January 2025, No. 2025-00715. Submitted to the Seimas by Government Resolution No. 860 of 16 October 2024. A parallel amendment to the Law on Information Society Services designates the Communications Regulatory Authority (RRT) as market surveillance authority.
instrument_date: Adopted 14 January 2025; published in the Register of Legal Acts (TAR) 22 January 2025; most substantive provisions in force from 1 April 2025
competent_authority: Innovation Agency (VšĮ Inovacijų agentūra), under the Ministry of the Economy and Innovation, establishes and operates the sandbox. RRT (Ryšių reguliavimo tarnyba) is the AI Act market surveillance authority and single point of contact (from 1 April 2025) and is a project partner supervising AI use inside the testing environment. The Innovation Agency is also the notifying authority (from 2 August 2025).
sectors_in_scope: No sector limitation stated. Targeted at Lithuanian micro, small and medium enterprises, with published priority for companies developing or deploying high-risk AI systems. No sectoral enumeration in the ministry or RRT material.
notes:
CODED IMPLEMENTING, NOT OPERATIONAL — but this is the closest call of the four and worth a second pass before it goes in the paper. The Ministry of the Economy and Innovation's sandbox page states verbatim that the Innovation Agency 'veiklas pradėjo vykdyti 2025 m. spalio mėnesį' (began carrying out activities in October 2025) and that 'pirmaisiais metais į programą pakviečiant dalyvauti 10 įmonių' (10 companies invited to participate in the first year), rising by 20 annually. It does NOT state that a cohort has been admitted, and no participant list or count is published anywhere I could find. Two separate reads of the same page produced conflicting summaries on this point, so I am treating admission as unconfirmed. RRT gives the project period as 30 October 2025 – 2 November 2028, EUR 3m from the ERDF.

IMPORTANT DEADLINE NOTE — this source is post-Omnibus and current: the ministry page states 'DI smėliadėžė turi būti sukurta ir pradėti veikti ne vėliau kaip 2027 m. rugpjūčio 2 d.' (the sandbox must be created and begin operating no later than 2 August 2027), correctly reflecting Regulation (EU) 2026/1744. Separately, Lithuanian law tasked the Agency to create a 'limited pilot AI regulation environment' (apribota bandomoji DI reglamentavimo aplinka) by 1 January 2026 — a national milestone distinct from the AI Act deadline. What began in October 2025 appears to be that national pilot precursor rather than the Art. 57 sandbox proper.

EXIT REPORT — do not code this as a yes without reading the statute. The ministry page says the Agency will give companies finishing the programme 'įvykdytų veiklų rašytinį įrodymą ir baigimo ataskaitą' (written evidence of activities carried out and a completion report) usable in conformity assessment. That is functionally the Art. 57(7) exit report, but it is described in a programme description, not shown to be a requirement of the national instrument. I could not confirm the sandbox provisions sit in Law No. XV-105 itself: an attempt to read the amending law and the consolidated Technology and Innovation Law via Infolex returned only the opening articles (paywalled), and the visible portion showed no sandbox provision. The instrument name and number above are confirmed; the location of the sandbox provision within it is NOT. Flag for a direct e-tar.lt/e-seimas read.

ENTRY CRITERIA — a published priority rule exists (high-risk AI developers/deployers, MSMEs) but no criteria set or application procedure was published on the ministry, RRT or Innovation Agency pages. Coded unknown rather than no.

derogation_power_note: Draft Art. 12 cross-refers to Chapter VI without conferring derogation power. Bill not adopted.
suff_graduation_note: Documented negative: draft Art. 12 contains no exit-report provision and cross-refers to Chapter VI. Statement about the draft, not about law in force.
suff_recognition_note: Draft Art. 12 cross-refers to Chapter VI of the Regulation as a whole.
legal_instrument: No national instrument in force. Projet de loi n° 8476 'portant mise en oeuvre de certaines dispositions du règlement (UE) 2024/1689' — approved by the Conseil de gouvernement 29 November 2024, deposited in the Chambre des Députés 23 December 2024, referred to the Commission des Médias et des Communications 16 January 2025, rapporteur Félix Eischen appointed 3 June 2025, Conseil d'État opinion received 10 July 2026. Status as of September 2026: still 'en commission', no plenary vote, NOT adopted. Article 12 of the bill carries the sandbox obligation.
instrument_date: Bill deposited 23 December 2024; Conseil d'État opinion 10 July 2026; not adopted as of 8 September 2026
competent_authority: Commission nationale pour la protection des données (CNPD) — designated in the bill as single point of contact, national coordinator of competent authorities, default/horizontal market surveillance authority for Annex III systems, and the body required to establish at least one AI regulatory sandbox. Other market surveillance authorities designated by domain: CSSF (financial), Commissariat aux Assurances (insurance), ILNAS (Annex I pts 1-10), ILR (critical infrastructure), ALMPS (Luxembourg medicines agency — Annex I pts 11-12, health products), ALIA (transparency/AI-generated content), plus a judicial control authority for AI used by courts.
sectors_in_scope: Article 12 names no sectors; it cross-refers to Chapter VI of Regulation (EU) 2024/1689. Market surveillance is split by sector across eight authorities, but the sandbox obligation itself sits with the CNPD alone and is not sector-scoped in the bill text.
notes:
DO NOT CONFLATE THE TWO LUXEMBOURG SANDBOXES — this is the trap in this record and it is exactly the kind of thing that would be a citable error. The CNPD has run an operational regulatory sandbox called 'Sandkëscht' since May 2024 (applications opened 14 June 2024), which tests new technologies and new uses of data 'notamment en intelligence artificielle' with GDPR compliance as its stated objective. The CNPD's own Sandkëscht page contains no mention of the AI Act, Article 57, or any 2026/2027 deadline. It is a data-protection sandbox that happens to take AI cases, NOT the Article 57 sandbox. A 20 January 2026 government/CNPD conference communiqué refers loosely to 'the CNPD's AI regulatory sandbox' as an existing innovation-support tool, which is where trackers coding Luxembourg as operational are almost certainly going wrong. Luxembourg has no Art. 57 sandbox running.

STALE DATE INSIDE THE BILL ITSELF: Article 12 reads 'La Commission nationale pour la protection des données met en place au moins un bac à sable réglementaire de l'IA selon les modalités visées au chapitre VI du règlement (UE) 2024/1689 au plus tard le 2 août 2026.' The bill was deposited December 2024, so this 2 August 2026 date predates Regulation (EU) 2026/1744 and is superseded by the 2 August 2027 deadline. Whether the deadline is corrected before adoption is unresolved and worth checking against the Conseil d'État opinion of 10 July 2026 — I did not read that opinion in full.

EXIT REPORT coded 'no' on a documented negative: Article 12 contains no exit-report provision and cross-refers to Chapter VI rather than restating Art. 57(7). Since the bill is not law, this is a statement about the draft, not about a national instrument in force.

The EC AI Act Service Desk national resources page lists NO designated authorities or implementing law for Luxembourg, consistent with the bill not having passed. The health angle: ALMPS is designated as market surveillance authority for Annex I points 11-12 (medical devices/IVDs), but that is enforcement, not sandbox scope — do not read it as health AI being in sandbox scope.

legal_instrument: Artificial Intelligence Regulations, 2025 — Legal Notice 226 of 2025, subsidiary legislation S.L. 591.05, made under the Malta Digital Innovation Authority Act (Cap. 591). Published in the Government Gazette of Malta No. 21,519 on 10 October 2025. The sandbox provision is Regulation 9 of S.L. 591.05. Companion instrument: Legal Notice 227 of 2025, Artificial Intelligence (Designation of the Information and Data Protection Commissioner for the purposes of Regulation (EU) 2024/1689) Regulations, 2025, made under the Data Protection Act.
instrument_date: 10 October 2025 (Government Gazette No. 21,519). MDIA enforcement powers stated to take effect 2 August 2026.
competent_authority: Malta Digital Innovation Authority (MDIA) — lead market surveillance authority, single point of contact for national AI governance, and the sole authority responsible for establishing and running the national AI regulatory sandbox (Reg. 9, S.L. 591.05). The Information and Data Protection Commissioner (IDPC) is designated under LN 227/2025 for data-protection/fundamental-rights functions. MDIA coordinates with the MFSA and other sectoral market surveillance bodies. MDIA states it works with DiHubMT to support SMEs and public sector bodies in sandbox participation.
sectors_in_scope: No sector limitation. MDIA's framework material covers the eight Annex III high-risk areas generically (biometrics, law enforcement, education, employment, etc.). Reg. 9 requires MDIA to give priority access to SMEs and start-ups with a registered office or branch in the EU — a participant-type priority, not a sectoral one.
notes:
MAJOR SOURCING CAVEAT — I could not read the text of LN 226/2025. legislation.mt returns only a metadata page to fetch tools and blocks direct download at the network layer (403 at the egress proxy on legislation.mt and justiceservices.gov.mt). Everything below the instrument's title, LN number, S.L. number, parent Act and Gazette date rests on MDIA's own site plus law-firm commentary (Chambers/GTG/BDO/LexMT), not the statute. Before this goes in the paper someone must open the LN 226 PDF directly and read Regulation 9. Specifically unresolved: whether Reg. 9 sets admission criteria, whether it names sectors, and whether it requires the Art. 57(7) exit report. I have coded all three unknown rather than guess.

What IS well-supported: MDIA's own services page states it is the sole authority responsible for establishing the national AI regulatory sandbox and that LN 226 of 2025 formally established these designations. LexMT independently identifies the provision as S.L. 591.05 Reg. 9 and reports the SME/start-up priority-access duty. Two independent sources agreeing on the S.L. citation is reasonable but not primary.

NOT OPERATIONAL: no launch announcement, no call for applications, no participant count, and no sandbox guidelines found on mdia.gov.mt as of September 2026. MDIA's homepage references its participation in the European Blockchain Regulatory Sandbox — that is DLT, not AI, and should not be miscoded. Malta is a designation-complete, not-yet-running case.

Date hygiene: MDIA's own timeline page gives 2 December 2027 for high-risk AI system requirements, which is consistent with the post-Omnibus schedule and suggests MDIA material is current rather than stale.

legal_instrument: No national instrument in force. Concept-Uitvoeringswet AI-verordening (UAIA) — draft implementing bill. Public internet consultation ran to 1 June 2026 (announced c. 20 April 2026); the Raad van State's Afdeling bestuursrechtspraak submitted its consultation response on 8 July 2026. As of September 2026 the bill has not been submitted to or passed by either chamber. The sandbox provision is Article 4.1 of the draft bill. A separate, earlier non-binding document exists: 'Vormvoorstel Nederlandse regulatory sandbox onder de AI-verordening', published 25 March 2025 by the Ministry of Economic Affairs with AP and RDI — a design proposal, NOT a legal instrument.
instrument_date: Design proposal 25 March 2025; consultation closed 1 June 2026; Raad van State consultation response 8 July 2026; no instrument adopted as of 8 September 2026
competent_authority: Not yet formally designated by law. Ten market surveillance authorities were announced by cabinet letter to the Tweede Kamer (State Secretary Willemijn Aerdts), with the Autoriteit Persoonsgegevens (AP) and the Rijksinspectie Digitale Infrastructuur (RDI) in coordinating roles. Under draft Article 4.1 the market surveillance authorities jointly establish the sandbox; the 2025 design proposal envisages a single multi-sectoral sandbox run by a coordinating 'Kernteam' with an expert pool of sectoral supervisors and 'intensive trajectories' for in-depth cases.
sectors_in_scope: All sectors covered by the AI Regulation, including general-purpose AI systems — the design proposal is explicit that the Netherlands intends ONE multi-sectoral sandbox rather than sectoral ones, with sector expertise supplied by the expert pool. No sector is singled out.
notes:
Confidence is high for the STATUS determination (no instrument in force, nothing running) because it rests on the Raad van State's own consultation page dated 8 July 2026 describing a conceptwetsvoorstel — a primary source and a documented negative. Confidence on the finer coding fields is lower; treat health_ai, exit_report and participants as genuinely open.

STALE-DATE WARNING ON THE 2025 DESIGN PROPOSAL: the Vormvoorstel of 25 March 2025 targets the sandbox being operational by August 2026 and states it was drawn up while the Commission's sandbox implementing acts were still unknown. Both premises are now obsolete — the deadline moved to 2 August 2027 under Regulation (EU) 2026/1744. Do not cite the Vormvoorstel for the deadline. Note the AP's hosted PDF of it returned 403 to my fetch; I read it via the RDI mirror of the same document.

NOTEWORTHY FOR THE PAPER, possibly for the governance argument rather than the coding table: the Raad van State's Chair of the Afdeling bestuursrechtspraak objected to the draft's requirement that the Division participate in the sandbox, on the ground that guiding sandbox participants on how to comply 'is not compatible with the independent judicial assessment' of compliance in individual cases. That is a live separation-of-functions objection to the Art. 57(7) guidance duty, raised by a supreme administrative court against its own government's implementing bill. It is a good, citable illustration of the institutional-conditions argument the manuscript is making — and it is about the guidance duty specifically, which is the same provision that carries the exit report.

I could not read draft Article 4.1 verbatim: internetconsultatie.nl is robots-disallowed to my fetch tool and two Dutch legal-commentary mirrors were blocked (robots/anti-bot). Whether Art. 4.1 restates the Art. 57(7) exit report is therefore unknown, not absent.

derogation_power_note: Art. 97(2) requires notification of the Commission and AI Board within 7 days of approving a sandbox exemption, implying a derogation mechanism, but Arts. 91-96 were not readable. Do not code yes without the statute text.
suff_funding_note: Funded in part by participant fees (reported 14,418 PLN general / 4,806 PLN local government, MSME exempt). Fee figures rest on a single outlet - re-verify before printing.
