legal_instrument: Ustawa z dnia 3 lipca 2026 r. o systemach sztucznej inteligencji (Act of 3 July 2026 on artificial intelligence systems), Dz.U. 2026 poz. 1003. Sandbox provisions sit in Chapter 7 "Środki wspierające innowacyjność" (Measures supporting innovation), Arts. 91–99; Art. 6 pkt 11 assigns KRiBSI the task of creating and managing regulatory sandboxes.
instrument_date: Adopted 3 July 2026; published in Dziennik Ustaw 27 July 2026 (Dz.U. 2026 poz. 1003); entered into force 11 August 2026 (14 days after publication), with a further tranche of provisions (individual opinions Arts. 8–18, inspection/enforcement/complaints chapters) applying from 28 October 2026.
competent_authority: Komisja Rozwoju i Bezpieczeństwa Sztucznej Inteligencji (KRiBSI) — Commission for the Development and Safety of Artificial Intelligence. KRiBSI establishes the sandbox, runs the selection competitions and supervises participants. Not yet constituted: the chair is to be appointed by 11 October 2026 and the full Commission is expected to begin work in November 2026.
sectors_in_scope: Not sector-limited. The Act does not enumerate sectors — the sandbox is open horizontally to AI providers/deployers, startups, micro/small/medium enterprises and local-government units (jednostki samorządu terytorialnego). No sectoral carve-in or carve-out identified in Arts. 91–99.
participants: 0 — none. The sandbox has not launched; KRiBSI does not yet exist and no competition round has been announced.
notes: Strongest case of the four. The national instrument is adopted, published and partly in force, and it contains a real sandbox regime rather than a placeholder. Verified from the statute's own article structure (Art. 6 pkt 11; Chapter 7, Arts. 91–99) via the lexlege mirror of the consolidated text and the infor.pl metryka for the Dz.U. citation; ISAP, eli.gov.pl, dziennikustaw.gov.pl and gov.pl were unreachable from this environment (robots.txt / egress policy), so I could not read the official PDF directly — the ISAP and ELI URLs are listed as the citation of record, not as pages I read. Flag this if the paper needs article text quoted verbatim. STATUS RATIONALE: 'implementing', not 'operational' — Deputy Minister Dariusz Standerski was quoted (rp.pl) saying launching the sandbox is 'a matter of three months' from the Commission's constitution, and the ministry intends to use that window for preparatory work. MECHANICS (from the statute as reported): participation is awarded through competitions (konkursy) organised and decided by KRiBSI, which publishes terms and selection criteria per round and produces a ranking list; applications carry technical system descriptions, product information and planned scope/reach; participation runs 6–12 months. Art. 97(1) has KRiBSI set the cap on affected users/entities and the scope of each project; Art. 97(2) requires notification of the European Commission and the AI Board within 7 days of approving a sandbox exemption; Art. 97(3) routes the Art. 57(16) reports onward. Art. 98 obliges the participant to file an ANNUAL progress report to KRiBSI and to publish notice of its sandbox participation on its website. Art. 99 gives KRiBSI inspection powers and an exclusion procedure (30-day remediation notice; exclusion resolution effective 14 days after service). EXIT REPORT — read carefully: I found NO provision in Arts. 91–99 codifying the Art. 57(7) exit report (the authority's written confirmation and detailed report of activities, results and learning outcomes issued TO the participant). Art. 98's annual report runs the other direction (participant to authority) and Art. 97(3) concerns Art. 57(16) reporting to the EU. Art. 57(7) is directly applicable regardless, so absence from the national text is not a legal gap — but do not code Poland 'yes' on this variable without reading Arts. 91–96 verbatim, which I could not access. Coded 'unknown' deliberately. FEES: reported by Forsal.pl as a one-off 14,418 PLN for general entities and 4,806 PLN for local-government units, with micro/small/medium enterprises exempt. The MŚP exemption is corroborated by rp.pl; the two PLN figures rest on Forsal alone — medium confidence, re-verify before printing a number. HEALTH: medical/health AI is not named anywhere in the sandbox chapter. Commentary (prawo.pl, 10 June 2026) uses a medical-device example only to make the point that MDR/IVDR obligations and full civil liability survive sandbox participation — illustrative commentary, not statutory scope; do not cite it as Poland naming health AI in scope.

legal_instrument: No national instrument establishing an AI Act Article 57 sandbox. The only national commitment found is Resolução do Conselho de Ministros n.º 2/2026, approving the Agenda Nacional de Inteligência Artificial 2026–2030, which lists "Definição de sandboxes regulatórias" as an action item in the 2026–2030 plan with no operating entity, criteria or timeline attached. Portugal separately has a pre-existing, general (non-AI-Act) sandbox regime — Decreto-Lei n.º 67/2021, de 30 de julho, on Zonas Livres Tecnológicas (ZLT), building on RCM n.º 29/2020, de 21 de abril — but neither ANI's ZLT programme nor any government source presents ZLT as Portugal's Article 57 sandbox.
instrument_date: RCM n.º 2/2026: adopted 8 January 2026, published/in force 9 January 2026. Decreto-Lei n.º 67/2021 (ZLT): 30 July 2021. No AI-Act-specific instrument as of 8 September 2026.
competent_authority: ANACOM (Autoridade Nacional de Comunicações) — announced by the Government on 19 September 2025 as national market surveillance authority and single point of contact, coordinating 14 sectoral bodies (Portugal has published its Art. 77 fundamental-rights authority list). No authority has been designated to operate a sandbox. Caveat: the formal instrument effecting the ANACOM designation has not been publicly identified — the Chambers Artificial Intelligence 2026 Portugal guide (as of May 2026) states expressly that the implementing act confirming the designation had not been publicly identified, while the CMS AI Regulation Scanner (updated 17 February 2026) calls the September 2025 designation 'formal'. Treat the designating instrument as unverified.
sectors_in_scope: Not defined for AI. RCM 2/2026 does not scope the planned sandboxes. For context only, the four existing ZLT are scoped to defence/security (Infante D. Henrique), carbon-neutral mobility (Matosinhos), 5G/IoT/autonomous vehicles/AI/cybersecurity (Aveiro) and ocean renewable energy (Viana do Castelo) — none health.
participants: unknown — no AI Act sandbox exists, so none. ZLT admissions are a separate, non-AI-Act programme; ANI's ZLT application process was listed as 'under maintenance'.
notes: CODING CALL: 'announced' rests on one thread only — RCM 2/2026's inclusion of 'Definição de sandboxes regulatórias' as an action in the National AI Agenda 2026–2030. That is a real government commitment in a published Council of Ministers resolution, clearing the 'public commitment, no instrument' bar, but it is thin: no operator, no timeline, no criteria. If your codebook requires the commitment to be sandbox-specific rather than a line item in a five-year strategy, 'nothing_reported' is also defensible. SOURCING CAVEAT: I could not read the full RCM 2/2026 text — diariodarepublica.pt is JavaScript-gated and anacom.pt returns 403 to automated fetches from this environment — so the 'Definição de Sandboxes regulatórias' wording comes from the CMS Portugal summary of the resolution, not from the Diário da República text itself. VERIFY THAT LINE VERBATIM before it carries weight in the paper; the diariodarepublica and digital.gov.pt URLs are the places to do it. TRAP TO AVOID: several sources conflate the Zonas Livres Tecnológicas regime (DL 67/2021) with an AI Act sandbox. They are distinct instruments with distinct legal bases; ANI's own ZLT page makes no reference to Article 57. Do not code Portugal 'implementing' on the strength of DL 67/2021. Portugal has enacted no dedicated AI Act implementing law as of the most recent sources checked (CMS, 17 Feb 2026; Chambers, May 2026; PwC Portugal, 2026). STALENESS FLAG: PwC's 2026 piece still describes sandboxes as something that 'must become available' from 2 August 2026 — that predates or ignores the Digital Omnibus; the live member-state deadline is 2 August 2027.

legal_instrument: None found. No lege, ordonanță de urgență (OUG) or hotărâre de guvern (HG) establishing an AI regulatory sandbox, and no national AI Act implementing legislation in force. The only national act located is a Government Memorandum proposing the institutional architecture (authorities under Arts. 70 and 77), which does not address Articles 57–63.
instrument_date: unknown — the Government Memorandum's date is not stated in ANCOM's own communication and I could not verify it from a primary source.
competent_authority: None designated for a sandbox, and none formally designated under Article 70. ANCOM (Autoritatea Națională pentru Administrare și Reglementare în Comunicații) is PROPOSED via the Government Memorandum as national market surveillance authority and single point of contact, alongside ASF and BNR (high-risk AI in financial services), ANSPDCP (biometric and law-enforcement AI) and sectoral bodies (ANPC, Inspecția Muncii). ANCOM states expressly that it and the other authorities cannot verify or sanction non-compliance until the national implementing act enters into force.
sectors_in_scope: unknown — no sandbox instrument exists.
participants: unknown — no sandbox exists, so none.
notes: Cleanest negative case of the four, confirmed from the regulator's own mouth. ANCOM's press release of 24 July 2026, 'Artificial Intelligence Act in Romania — current state of the implementation framework', says national implementing legislation is still being drafted, lists only the Memorandum-proposed authorities, and contains NO mention whatsoever of an Article 57 sandbox — not planned, not funded, not timed. Independent Romanian coverage through July–August 2026 (Agerpres, Economedia, Bursa, Edupedu, juridice.ro) describes a 'vid legislativ' in which the AI Act applies but is nationally unenforceable, and none reports a sandbox. Romania missed the 2 August 2025 Art. 70 designation deadline. Note the two sources I could not open directly: juridice.ro returned 403 and hategan.ro failed robots.txt from this environment, so the Romanian legal-commentary side rests on edupedu.ro, money.ro and the ANCOM release; juridice.ro is listed as the citation to verify rather than a page I read. HISTORICAL THREAD IF YOU NEED IT: an October 2025 MIAI/ai-regulation.com survey states Romania had submitted a draft AI bill to Parliament that drew majority-negative opinions in the legislative procedure for failing to address AI Act implementation adequately; by July 2026 ANCOM describes drafting as still under way, suggesting that earlier bill did not survive. I did not verify that bill's number or fate — if the paper wants Romania's legislative history rather than current state, check the Camera Deputaților and Senat registers, which were not reachable here. CONFIDENCE NOTE: high confidence that nothing is reported — a distinct claim from high confidence that nothing exists, though a national sandbox operating without the market surveillance authority mentioning it in a July 2026 status release is implausible.

suff_funding_note: Impact statement carries EUR 8.24m and 68 new public-sector posts, of which EUR 6.28m is unfunded; bill not enacted. Sources disagree on the year - verify the dolozka vplyvov.
legal_instrument: Návrh zákona o štátnej správe v oblasti umelej inteligencie a európskej dátovej regulácie (draft Act on state administration in the field of artificial intelligence and European data regulation) — a GOVERNMENT BILL, approved by the Government of the Slovak Republic but NOT enacted. Not yet passed by the National Council (NR SR) and not published in the Zbierka zákonov, so it carries no law number. Earlier-stage title in circulation: 'návrh zákona o organizácii štátnej správy v oblasti umelej inteligencie'.
instrument_date: Approved by the Government on 26 August 2026. Proposed entry into force: 1 January 2027. Preceded by inter-ministerial comment procedure (pripomienkové konanie) and Legislative Council of the Government review during mid-2026. No NR SR vote confirmed as of 8 September 2026.
competent_authority: MIRRI SR — Ministerstvo investícií, regionálneho rozvoja a informatizácie Slovenskej republiky. Under the bill MIRRI would be the general AI market surveillance authority and single point of contact, would act as data coordinator, and is expressly tasked with establishing, operating and developing the regulačné experimentálne prostredie (regulatory experimental environment / sandbox). Sectoral supervision would be split with NBÚ, the Úrad na ochranu osobných údajov, the Úrad inšpekčnej služby and the Ministry of Justice. The designation takes legal effect only on the law's entry into force — Slovakia had made no public Art. 70 designation as of the August 2025 deadline.
sectors_in_scope: Not defined. The bill does not enumerate sectors for the sandbox; the provision is drafted at a high level of generality.
participants: 0 — none. No sandbox exists; the enabling law is not in force.
notes: CODING CALL — read before using: applying your rubric strictly ('implementing' = legal instrument PASSED or authority DESIGNATED), Slovakia is 'announced' — the bill is government-approved but not enacted, and MIRRI's designation has no legal effect until 1 January 2027 at the earliest. A looser reading that counts cabinet approval of a bill naming an operator as 'implementing' is arguable; if your codebook sets the threshold there, recode. I chose the conservative code. Flag the borderline in the coding appendix: Slovakia and Portugal both sit near whatever line you draw and a reviewer will probe it. SUBSTANCE WORTH CITING: Slovak practitioner commentary (Prosman & Pavlovič) criticises the sandbox provision as normatively empty — the draft 'essentially limits itself to a general statement' and does not resolve data handling, cybersecurity requirements, separation of testing from production, or an implementation timeline. That is a quotable data point for an argument that Article 57 transposition is being done thinly, and it is a lawyers' reading of the bill text rather than a tracker summary. FISCAL DETAIL: the impact statement carries €8.24m and 68 new public-sector posts (reported for 2026 by info.sk and for 2027 by teraz.sk — the two outlets disagree on the year, so do not print a year without checking the doložka vplyvov), with €6.28m unfunded. SOURCING CAVEAT: mirri.gov.sk and skubla.sk were unreachable from this environment (robots.txt / connect failures) and are listed as citations to verify, not pages I read; the bill's exact title, the 26 August 2026 approval date and the 1 January 2027 effective date rest on Slovak press (teraz.sk/TASR, info.sk, openiazoch.zoznam.sk) plus law-firm commentary. Pull the parlamentná tlač number from the NR SR register and the doložka before citing. EXIT REPORT: nothing in any source indicates the bill codifies Art. 57(7); given the criticism that the provision is a bare general statement it very likely does not — but 'unknown' is the honest code without the bill text.

suff_graduation_note: An annual duty tied to Art. 57(16) surfaced; no Art. 57(7) clause surfaced. Art. 17 ZIUDHPUI was not read in full.
legal_instrument: Zakon o izvajanju uredbe (EU) o določitvi harmoniziranih pravil o umetni inteligenci (ZIUDHPUI), Uradni list RS, št. 85/2025. The sandbox provision is Article 17, implementing Art. 57 of Regulation (EU) 2024/1689.
instrument_date: Published in Uradni list RS on 6 November 2025 (Uradni list RS št. 85/2025). Exact adoption date in the Državni zbor and entry-into-force date not independently verified.
competent_authority: Agencija za komunikacijska omrežja in storitve Republike Slovenije (AKOS) — Agency for Communication Networks and Services. AKOS coordinates with notified bodies, market surveillance authorities and sectoral inspectorates for the specific domain chosen.
sectors_in_scope: Not yet fixed. ZIUDHPUI Art. 17 provides that the sandbox's substantive domain is chosen by AKOS via a public call (javni poziv), with selection criteria including the number of similar proposals in a content area, the number of AI technologies within it, expected societal impact and alignment with the public interest, and a higher risk level of the AI use. The competent ministry may also designate a domain directly on public-interest grounds.
participants: unknown — no admitted participants reported. AKOS had issued a public call inviting the public to propose the sandbox's content area, but I could not establish the call's opening date, deadline, or outcome from a primary source.
notes: The instrument and the competent authority are solid: ZIUDHPUI, Uradni list RS 85/2025, AKOS, sandbox at Art. 17. Everything downstream is thin. (1) Slovenia uses a two-stage design that is distinctive and worth noting in the paper: a first public call selects the sandbox's *subject-matter domain*, and only then does a second open call invite candidates to test AI systems within it. Participant-level entry criteria therefore cannot exist until stage one closes — hence entry_criteria_published = no rather than unknown. Published so far is only an outline: priority and free access for startups and SMEs. (2) Exit report: the Uradni-list reading I obtained surfaced an annual reporting duty tied to Art. 57(16) of the AI Act, and did not surface an Art. 57(7) exit-report clause. I am not confident either way — I could not read the full text of Art. 17 (WebFetch session limit hit). Marked unknown; the fix is a direct read of Art. 17 ZIUDHPUI on uradni-list.si or pisrs.si. (3) STALENESS FLAG relevant to the paper: AKOS's own English sandbox page still states the establishment deadline as 2 August 2026, i.e. it has not been updated for Regulation (EU) 2026/1744. Treat any date framing on that page as pre-Omnibus. (4) Health/medical AI is not named anywhere I found; do not infer it from the general framing.

verification_note: Pre-AI-Act precursor scheme under RD 817/2023. Sunsets ~Nov 2026 per the RD's own vigencia clause; the Art. 57-native instrument remains an unenacted bill.
derogation_power_note: RD 817/2023 creates a controlled compliance-testing environment against the then-proposed Regulation; no power to disapply national rules.
suff_graduation_note: Art. 23 RD 817/2023 is bidirectional: participants report to the Subdireccion General, and the authority issues a participation certificate plus an evaluation report. Those are documents, not instruments carrying weight in a conformity procedure.
suff_recognition_note: RD 817/2023 predates the Regulation and cannot reference Art. 58.
legal_instrument: Real Decreto 817/2023, de 8 de noviembre, por el que se establece un entorno controlado de pruebas para el ensayo del cumplimiento de la propuesta de Reglamento ... en materia de inteligencia artificial (BOE-A-2023-22767, published BOE 9 Nov 2023). NOTE: an Article 57-native instrument is still pending — Proyecto de Ley Orgánica para el buen uso y la gobernanza de la inteligencia artificial, approved by the Consejo de Ministros 26 May 2026 and under parliamentary consideration as BOCG-15-A-97-1 (expediente 121/000096); not enacted as of 8 Sept 2026.
instrument_date: 8 November 2023 (RD 817/2023); pending Ley Orgánica approved as a bill 26 May 2026
competent_authority: Secretaría de Estado de Digitalización e Inteligencia Artificial (SEDIA), Ministerio para la Transformación Digital y de la Función Pública, named as 'órgano competente' in RD 817/2023. AESIA (Agencia Española de Supervisión de la Inteligencia Artificial, created by RD 729/2023) is the designated AI supervisory agency and is the expected operator under the pending Ley Orgánica — but the sandbox cohort actually run in 2025 was administered by SEDIA. Do not attribute the 2025 cohort to AESIA without further checking.
sectors_in_scope: RD 817/2023 annex lists eight Annex-III-style high-risk areas (biometrics; critical infrastructure; education and vocational training; employment and worker management; access to essential public and private services; law enforcement; migration/asylum/border control; administration of justice and democratic processes). In practice the admitted cohort spans essential services, biometrics, employment, critical infrastructure, machinery, medical devices (productos sanitarios) and in vitro diagnostic medical devices.
participants: 12 high-risk AI systems, provisionally selected from 44 applications (call closed 30 January 2025; cohort work began April 2025). Two are medical-device systems: CL@UDIA and Tucuvi Health Manager.
adversarial_verification: UNVERIFIED — verify agent did not run
notes: Facts on the 2025 cohort are well sourced; the characterisation is the delicate part and matters for the paper. (1) RD 817/2023 predates the AI Act and is expressly framed as testing compliance with the *proposal* for the AI Regulation; it is time-limited to a maximum of 36 months from entry into force or until the AI Act becomes applicable in Spain. So Spain's running sandbox is best described as a transitional/precursor scheme that in practice satisfies the Art. 57 function, not a sandbox created under a national Art. 57 transposition. If the paper codes Spain as 'operational under Art. 57' that claim should be hedged. (2) Exit report: Art. 23 RD 817/2023 obliges participants to submit a report to the competent body on exit, with content specified in guidance the competent body issues. That is a participant-to-authority report, which is NOT the same direction of obligation as Art. 57(7), where the sandbox authority provides an exit report to the participant. Coded 'yes' because a national exit-report obligation exists, but the Art. 57(7)-specific mapping is unverified — recommend reading Arts. 22-23 of the RD directly before citing. (3) The first cohort's testing phase concluded and 15 guidance documents (2 general + 13 technical) plus compliance checklists were published on 11 December 2025; no second call was confirmed as of Sept 2026. (4) A Moncloa release also gives entity counts (18 SMEs, 6 startups) that do not reconcile cleanly with '12 systems' — likely counting consortium members; do not cite the entity counts without verifying. (5) I could not retrieve the BOE full text or the digital.gob.es 'Resultados' page directly (robots/proxy blocks and a WebFetch session limit), so the RD annex list and Art. 23 wording come from one WebFetch of the BOE diario page plus corroborating Spanish legal commentary — worth one direct re-read of BOE-A-2023-22767 before submission.

legal_instrument: No enacted national instrument establishing the sandbox. Two things exist instead: (a) a government assignment (regeringsuppdrag) of June 2026, 'Uppdrag att vara nationella behöriga myndigheter enligt AI-förordningen', tasking Post- och telestyrelsen (PTS), Integritetsskyddsmyndigheten (IMY), Finansinspektionen, Läkemedelsverket and Swedac with acting as national competent authorities on an interim basis, reported as running through 31 December 2026, with PTS given responsibility for establishing the mandatory regulatory sandbox; and (b) SOU 2025:101, 'Anpassningar till AI-förordningen – Säker användning, effektiv kontroll och stöd för innovation' (6 October 2025), a public inquiry proposing a new Swedish act and ordinance with PTS as the sandbox authority — still at consultation/remiss stage, not law.
instrument_date: SOU 2025:101 published 6 October 2025; government assignment dated June 2026 (exact day and diarienummer not confirmed)
competent_authority: Post- och telestyrelsen (PTS) — assigned lead responsibility for the AI Act in Sweden and specifically for establishing the regulatory sandbox. IMY is the market surveillance authority for its areas; Läkemedelsverket is the competent authority for AI in medical devices, but that is a market-surveillance role, not sandbox operation.
sectors_in_scope: Not specified. PTS describes an intended cross-sector sandbox open to Swedish companies from startups to large industrial firms and to public-sector actors, with other agencies drawn in for data protection, GDPR and transparency questions. No sectoral scoping decision has been published.
participants: unknown — none. Applications are not open; PTS is running a stakeholder survey to inform the sandbox's design.
notes: Sweden is the clearest 'implementing, not operational' case of the three. As of the PTS sandbox page's last update on 27 July 2026, PTS was in the planning phase, admission criteria were explicitly still to be defined, and no application process had been announced. (1) Sweden has NO enacted national sandbox instrument — code legal_instrument as 'none found' if the paper's coding scheme requires an enacted law; the June 2026 regeringsuppdrag is an administrative assignment, not legislation, and it is time-limited. (2) A common error to avoid: several secondary sources present IMY as Sweden's AI Act authority generally. IMY is a market surveillance authority; the sandbox sits with PTS. Both statements appear on the respective agencies' own sites and are not in conflict once the roles are separated. (3) The June 2026 government decision is sourced to regeringen.se's regeringsuppdrag listing plus a Swedish law-firm summary; I did not read the decision text itself, so the 31 December 2026 end date and the precise list of five agencies should be confirmed against the regeringen.se document before citation. (4) Useful corroboration on the Omnibus for the paper: IMY's own AI Act page states the sandbox deadline is extended to 2 August 2027 and that high-risk obligations shift from 2 August 2026 — a national-authority primary source confirming the post-Omnibus timeline. (5) Exit report: unknown by construction, since no national instrument exists to impose one.
